The air was thick with the earthy aroma of wet soil, mingling with the sharp scent of acrid smoke that spiraled from the remnants of a smoldering campfire. Carys knelt in the underbrush, her fingertips tracing the frayed edges of a tattered map, its ink smudged and fading under the dappled light filtering through the trees. The forest pulsated around her, leaves rustling softly, carrying secrets that danced just beyond her grasp. The sun hung low, casting beams that pierced through the branches, illuminating the tiny motes of dust swirling lazily in the stillness.

“I swear, if we don’t find it soon, I’m going to lose my mind,” Jace muttered from a few paces away, his voice low yet laced with humor. She glanced up to see him leaning against a gnarled tree, arms crossed tightly across his chest, the muscles in his jaw tightening as he scanned the horizon. It was a familiar sight—his bravado barely masking the impatience simmering beneath the surface.

Carys smirked, tucking a loose strand of hair behind her ear as she met his gaze. “You mean you’re not already?” The playful challenge in her voice ignited a spark in his narrowed eyes. He was all too easy to provoke, and the banter felt like a tether, anchoring her amidst the uncertainty of their search.

“Ha, very funny.” Jace pushed himself off the tree, his boots crunching softly against the twigs and leaves as he strode toward her, each step an assertion of his presence. He leaned closer, glancing down at the map spread out on the ground, his frown deepening. “We’ve been at this for hours. What makes you think we’re even close?”
